newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stocks end firm on strong buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Athens stocks end firm on strong buying interest.

text.p: Athens stocks ended 0.63 percent up on Wednesday on heavy volume with analysts saying that despite profit taking the general share index ended higher because of excess demand for Greek equities.

"I had expected a weaker market on Wednesday. However the index closed 0.63 percent up and showed it could sustain profit taking without falling," said Evrikos Sarsentis, an analyst at Telesis Securities.
Foreign and Greek demand for stocks exceeded supply from investors who had already enjoyed high capital gains and were collecting profits, he said.

"The January rally had started with foreign funds, mainly interested in banks and large-caps. Now, there is an across-the-board investment focus and Greek retail investors and mutual funds have entered the bourse," he added.
Sarsentis expected the market to consolidate around 1,200-1,250 points in the next two sessions but saw a new rise before the end of February.
Promising sectors are those of construction and metallurgical companies, whose prospects are the strongest, he said.
The Athens general share index finished 0.63 percent or 7.78 points higher at 1252.37 points from Tuesday's 1244.59, after opening at 1242.58.
Losers led gainers 107 to 122 with 26 issues unchanged on 255 traded. Turnover was 20.2 billion drachmas on volume of 6.0 million shares.
Banking shares rallied with a 1.67 rise but construction shares lost 0.89 percent. Industrials closed down 0.65 percent.
Leasing shares gained 0.61 percent. Insurance lost 0.49 percent and small-caps dropped 0.55 percent.
